Open‑source maintainers are drawing a hard line: 22 high‑profile repositories have officially banned any contribution that originates from large language models.  

Together these projects hold more than 400 000 stars on GitHub, with immich (118 789 stars) and MeiliSearch (59 840 stars) accounting for roughly 45 % of that total.  

The bans cover every type of contribution—code, tests, documentation, PR descriptions, issue bodies, and even comments—generated by tools such as GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or Cursor, and are enforced by automated policy checks that reject the pull request outright.  

“Any content generated by generative AI tooling … will be rejected.”  

These restrictions aim to protect code quality, security, and licensing compliance, especially in critical components like search back‑ends, networking libraries, and system‑level software.  

The data reflects a rapid response, with all policies verified between 12 October 2026 and 11 November 2026, showing how quickly the community has moved to formalize these bans.
